sections.kicker: One familiar creative workspace / any production pipeline
sections.title:
Your tools will change.
Your workspace shouldn’t.
sections.lead: N’Brain gives creative teams a consistent place to direct work, review assets and control a production. Its modular UI can be shaped for a client, director or operator, while the digital double and orchestration connect the tools, APIs, AI models and compute behind it.
sections.micro: For film, previs, virtual production and live shows · across locations and devices

figure.alt: Concept illustration: one familiar creative workspace, with the tools, APIs and models behind it changing over time.

sections.title: A production should move at the speed of your creativity.
sections.lead: An idea can arrive as a sentence, a spoken direction, a movement or a cue. The production slows when that intent has to be translated by hand across interfaces, files and devices. N’Brain keeps the project context available as the crew works.

items.title: Stop switching modes of thought
items.text: Speak, move or use a controller without rebuilding the task inside another specialist interface.

items.title: Keep the context
items.text: Assets, shots, versions and decisions remain attached to the production, even when a tool changes.

items.title: Connect the action
items.text: Commands from devices and APIs reach the right project action through roles and permissions.

sections.answer: Express the idea in your own way. Keep a familiar workspace as the pipeline evolves.

sections.title:
Same creative experience.
Whatever comes next.
sections.lead: Six months from now, a production might replace an editor, add a new AI model or change an API. The creative team still enters through the same workspace, recognises the same project and finds its assets, devices and decisions in context.
sections.statement: The interface is the constant. N’Brain adapts the connections behind it.

sections.kicker: The main concept / the digital double
sections.title:
The project is a living double,
not a collection of exports.
sections.lead: A production exists in two worlds: the real venue or set, and its scripts, plans, 3D scenes, renders and cues. N’Brain binds them through a shared dataset so the crew and its agents can act on the same reality.

figure.alt: Real scans, LiDAR, maps and photos feed one digital double dataset. A 2D plan, 3D stage, LED pixel map, camera plates and show cues are connected views, with precise data flowing back to the real production.
figure.caption: The digital double is production data, not a 3D model exported once.

body: A conventional model is a snapshot. Once it is exported and imported into another tool, it can drift from the venue. Here dimensions, positions, cameras, screens and even the video on an LED wall remain attached to the project’s shared data.

The 2D plan, 3D stage, LED processor pixel map, camera plates and show cues become views of that data. Change the double and the real team receives the relevant numbers; measure a change on site and the double can update. An AI agent sees the stage and shot context instead of guessing from a prompt.

sections.kicker: How the promise works / three layers
sections.title:
The front end stays familiar.
N’Brain makes the rest flexible.
sections.lead: The UI gives creatives a consistent way to work with the digital double, assets and devices. N’Brain translates intent into actions across connected tools and compute. The data layer preserves project truth as those connections change.

figure.alt: Three-layer system map: creative control and Show Control above; N’Brain central orchestration with inputs, tools, APIs and compute; knowledge and production data below.
figure.caption: System map · all routes are coordinated from the N’Brain core.

layers.title: Show Control + widgets
layers.text: One workspace across desktop, tablet and phone. Modular widgets can form a simple review screen or a technical dashboard. Edit and Live modes accept voice, mocap, MIDI, OSC, gamepad and HTTP input.

layers.title: Agents and orchestration
layers.text: Agents read the show, coordinate tools and APIs, and propose or execute work through typed decisions and approval gates.

layers.title: Knowledge and production data
layers.text: Per-project memory, the double, scripts, shots, takes and versions stay structured. Lore tracks versions; every take belongs to its shot.

planes.title: Creative work has time to think.
planes.text: The control plane can ask for approval, use AI and take seconds. Its decisions do not block deterministic show operation.

planes.title: Live paths stay deterministic.
planes.text: Telemetry, cues, LED and cameras run on a separate data plane. No LLM sits in the hot path. Timing depends on the live configuration.

sections.note: The layers communicate through narrow, typed surfaces. Data can remain on the production’s machines; agents can use local GPUs or cloud engines. The existing design also describes signed 24-hour offline grants or full cloud hosting.

sections.title: Traditional craft, AI and virtual production in one thread.
sections.lead: “Hybrid” describes the work itself. A real location, AI-assisted assets and a virtual production stage contribute to the same shot. The crew does not have to reconstruct the brief, camera plan, versions and approvals at each handoff.

figure.alt: A car scene combines traditional location survey and camera work, AI-assisted environment and plate creation, and previs on an LED stage, converging on one shot and digital double.
figure.caption: A car scene is one example. Film, VAD, previs and live shows can connect different crafts around the same project data.

points.title: Traditional stays essential
points.text: Locations, performers, lenses, camera movement and physical takes ground the project.

points.title: AI has production context
points.text: Agents and generation work from the scene, shot, assets and constraints instead of a detached prompt.

points.title: Virtual production carries it to set
points.text: Previs, 3D stage, LED plates and cues stay tied to the same approved shot.

sections.note: This is hybrid production. Local/offline and online/cloud are separate deployment choices shown later; either mode can support a hybrid creative workflow.

sections.title: Speak it. Move it. Play it. Cue it.
sections.lead: The front end brings the project, its assets, metadata and connected devices into one coherent experience. Voice chat, camera gestures, mocap, a gamepad, Stream Deck, MIDI, OSC and HTTP requests offer different ways to express intent.
body: The director can work hands-free, the operator can use tactile controls, and software can send requests. N’Brain relates each input to the current project, role and authorised action.
sections.note: Input mappings and available modes depend on the production configuration. The deterministic live path does not wait for an AI model.

sections.title:
Keep the show on site.
Extend it online when you choose.
sections.lead: For a large show, the network may be unreliable and production data may need to remain private. N’Brain can run supported AI and distribute rendering on local machines without internet. When connected and authorised, the same project can also use online models, APIs and cloud render capacity—or mix local and cloud resources task by task.
sections.caption: Two deployment paths, with a hybrid choice within the same project.

paths.title: Operate on site.
paths.text: Supported AI and render jobs use production-owned hardware. Sensitive data and show control can stay on site, including when internet is unavailable. Offline operation follows the configured signed grant.

figure.alt: Concept illustration: AI and render jobs running on production-owned hardware on site, with no internet connection.

paths.title: Add connected capacity.
paths.text: Use authorised cloud models, APIs and render nodes when a connection is available. A hybrid production can choose local or cloud resources per task while keeping one workspace and project record.

figure.alt: Concept illustration: render routes from one project to local workstations and authorised cloud capacity, chosen per task.

sections.mini: Cloud compute and third-party APIs have separate usage costs. Customer-owned local hardware remains the customer’s capacity.

sections.title:
Choose where the work runs.
Control where the data goes.
sections.lead: The local/offline path gives a production a deliberate choice about environmental impact and confidentiality. Cloud remains available for the work that benefits from it.

values.title: Use compute deliberately.
values.main: Cloud AI and rendering draw on data-centre compute, cooling and network infrastructure. For suitable workloads, efficient local inference can avoid remote processing and repeated transfers while using hardware already on site.
items: Route supported tasks locally when that fits the job.
Use cloud capacity when its scale or capabilities are needed.
Compare actual energy and hardware use before making savings claims.

figure.alt: Concept illustration: routing suitable compute locally to use energy and hardware deliberately.

values.title: Keep confidential work under your control.
values.main: In local/offline mode, unreleased scripts, product designs, brand plans, talent likenesses and project metadata can remain on infrastructure controlled by the production.
items: Supported local models can run without sending content to a third-party AI server.
Choose which assets, if any, are allowed through connected APIs or cloud render paths.
Keep visibility over data routing and external service terms.

figure.alt: Concept illustration: confidential production material kept on infrastructure the production controls.

sections.foot: Local hardware still consumes electricity and has an equipment footprint. Privacy and legal duties still apply; connected-service configuration determines which data leaves the facility.

sections.title:
Keep every decision in reach.
Replay the story of a show.
sections.lead: N’Brain can record the production as it happens: scripts, assets, takes, approvals, cues, device events and results. Versions remain traceable through the project. A recorded show process can be revisited or replayed from its states and actions, while earlier configurations remain available to restore.

figure.alt: Production records and versions form an archive. A recorded show sequence can be replayed or restored; a separate consolidation path selects only relevant facts and asset references for an agent or tool.
figure.caption: Full production history and focused task context serve different purposes.

sections.answer: A chat holds a conversation. N’Brain keeps the production record.

benefits.title: Archive the whole process
benefits.text: Follow what changed, who approved it, which asset or take was used, and which cues or devices were involved. Replay a recorded show sequence for review and preparation.

benefits.title: Consolidate the working set
benefits.text: Smart tools gather the versions, references and results required for the next stage while the versioned archive remains accessible.

benefits.title: Spend context where it counts
benefits.text: Agents receive the relevant project facts for a task instead of the entire chat history each time. Reusing structured context can reduce repeated tokens and redundant active storage.

sections.note: Token and disk savings depend on the workflow, model and retention policy. The archive is preserved; consolidation changes what is active and passed to a task.
